title: Tiempos narrativos: past perfect y past perfect continuous

rule.title: Past perfect and narrative tenses
rule.explanation:
El past perfect («had» + participio) cuenta algo que pasó antes de otro momento del pasado:
- «When we arrived, the band had already started.» (primero empezó el grupo, luego llegamos)
- «I had never seen so many people before.»

Para contar historias combinamos tres tiempos:
- past simple para los hechos principales: «We arrived late.»
- past continuous para la situación de fondo: «Everyone was singing.»
- past perfect para lo que pasó antes: «Daniel had left the tickets at home.»

El past perfect continuous («had been» + «-ing») cuenta una acción que duraba hasta un momento del pasado, o que explica cómo estaba alguien:
- «The band had been playing for an hour when the electricity went off.»
- «Sam was tired because he had been practising all day.»

Palabras frecuentes: «already», «never… before», «by the time», «just», «because».

Ojo: si las acciones van en orden, basta el past simple: «I got up, had a shower and left». El past perfect se usa para volver atrás en la historia.

rows: They had been playing for an hour.

sets.instructions: Completa con el past perfect u otro tiempo pasado.

items.sentence: When we arrived, the band ___ already started.
Daniel had ___ the tickets at home. (leave)
He had never ___ in front of so many people. (play)
When I got home, Priya ___ gone to bed.
I had never ___ him so happy before. (see)
Everyone ___ singing when the lights went off.
The band had ___ playing for an hour when the electricity went off.
Sam was tired because he ___ been practising all day.
By the time we got to the station, the train ___ left.
She ___ been waiting for two hours when he finally arrived.
I couldn't get in because I ___ lost my keys.
We ___ dinner when the phone rang. (have, en curso)
They were wet because they had been ___ in the rain. (walk)

items.question: Cuando llegamos, el concierto ya había empezado.
options: When we arrived, the concert had already started.
When we arrived, the concert already started.
items.explanation: Lo que pasó antes: past perfect.

items.question: Nunca había visto tanta gente.
options: I had never seen so many people.
I have never seen so many people before that day.
items.explanation: Antes de otro momento pasado: past perfect.

items.question: Llevaban una hora tocando cuando se fue la luz.
options: They had been playing for an hour when the lights went off.
They have been playing for an hour when the lights went off.

items.question: Estaba cansado porque había estado ensayando.
options: He was tired because he had been practising.
He was tired because he has practised.

items.question: Me levanté, me duché y salí.
options: I got up, had a shower and left.
I had got up, had had a shower and had left.

items.question: Cuando llegué a casa, Priya se había acostado.
options: When I got home, Priya had gone to bed.
When I got home, Priya went to bed before.
items.explanation: Lo que pasó antes: past perfect.

items.question: Todos estaban cantando.
options: Everyone was singing.
Everyone had sang.

items.question: Para cuando llegamos, el tren se había ido.
options: By the time we arrived, the train had left.
By the time we arrived, the train has left.

items.question: Había olvidado las entradas.
options: He had forgotten the tickets.
He had forgot the tickets.

items.question: Estaban mojados porque habían estado andando bajo la lluvia.
options: They were wet because they had been walking in the rain.
They were wet because they walked in the rain now.
